document_title: A machine reads it first. How Texas scores written STAAR
_note: Slide strings set from the storyboard dossiers; each carries its claim ids.
caption:
Who reads a long written STAAR answer first?

Unless the test is in Spanish, a machine does. The Texas Education Agency has done it that way since December 2023. In the agency's chart the machine's score stands on about 75% of them. The agency said scoring them all by hand would have cost $15 million to $20 million more a year.

The machine learned from about 3,000 human scored answers per question. Low confidence scores, blank answers and a random sample go to people, and the person's score counts.

The agency said about 27,200 students got more credit on the reading test after content experts reread short typed answers. It said the engine scored none of them.

A parent can take a concern to the district. Its testing staff can request a human rescore for a fee. If the score changes, the fee is waived.

Should a family have to ask for a person?

#STAAR #TexasEducationAgency #TexasSchools

S1.headline: A machine reads it first.
S1.cite: c1 c17 c2 c14 c22 DRAWN
S1.body: Since December 2023 the Texas Education Agency has sent the longer written STAAR answers to an automated engine first, unless the test is in Spanish. The agency said scoring every answer by hand would have cost $15 million to $20 million more a year.
strings: Since December 2023 the Texas Education Agency has sent the longer written STAAR answers to an automated engine first, unless the test is in Spanish. The agency said scoring every answer by hand would have cost $15 million to $20 million more a year.

S2.headline: About 3,000 answers taught it.
S2.body: For each question the engine is programmed on about 3,000 field test answers that people scored. The agency requires it to agree with scorers as often as scorers agree with each other.
strings: For each question the engine is programmed on about 3,000 field test answers that people scored. The agency requires it to agree with scorers as often as scorers agree with each other.

S3.headline: About 75% keep the machine's score.
S3.body: In the agency's own chart the engine sets the score of record on about 75% of answers. Two people read the rest. A person's score is the one that counts.
strings: In the agency's own chart the engine sets the score of record on about 75% of answers. Two people read the rest. A person's score is the one that counts.

S4.headline: Low confidence scores go to people.
S4.cite: c33 c34 c6 c7 c32 DRAWN
S4.body: So do answers that are blank, too short, in another language, off topic or worded unlike the answers the engine learned from. So does a random sample.
strings: Low confidence scores go to people.
So do answers that are blank, too short, in another language, off topic or worded unlike the answers the engine learned from. So does a random sample.

S5.headline: Spanish STAAR answers skip the machine.
S5.body: Written answers on the Spanish language STAAR are 100 percent human scored.
strings: Spanish STAAR answers skip the machine.
Written answers on the Spanish language STAAR are 100 percent human scored.

S6.headline: About 1.7% of exams improved.
S6.body: Officials reviewed more than 1.6 million exams. Content experts reread the answers typed as a number, word or phrase. About 17 of every 1,000 improved.
strings: Officials reviewed more than 1.6 million exams. Content experts reread the answers typed as a number, word or phrase. About 17 of every 1,000 improved.

S7.headline: The agency says the engine scored none of the regraded answers.
S7.cite: c20 c19 c21 c23 c22 DRAWN
S7.body: About 27,200 students got more credit on the reading test after content experts reread short typed answers, like "ferst" for "first." That says nothing about how often the engine's own scores would change.
strings: The agency says the engine scored none of the regraded answers.

About 27,200 students got more credit on the reading test after content experts reread short typed answers, like "ferst" for "first." That says nothing about how often the engine's own scores would change.

S8.headline: Start with the district.
S8.body: A rescore can start with a parent or guardian's concern about a score. Rescores are read by people.
strings: A rescore can start with a parent or guardian's concern about a score. Rescores are read by people.

S9.headline: Ask the district for a rescore.
S9.body: District testing staff request it for a fee, inside a window set in the agency's Calendar of Events. If the score changes, the fee is waived.
strings: Ask the district for a rescore.
District testing staff request it for a fee, inside a window set in the agency's Calendar of Events. If the score changes, the fee is waived.
